jordan: quick drop: QuillMark-v3 embedding onboard finished. ran fp16, int8_pc, and int6_pc on wikismall + shorttail holdout. posting numbers + observations for triage.

jordan: TL;DR: overall r@5 and r@10 stable; r@1 gap concentrated on <=5-token queries. int6_pc narrows the r@1 gap vs int8_pc but increases norm variance. potential mitigations below.

mei: nice. paste the eval flags and dataset sizes?

jordan: eval flags: --model quillmark-v3 --quant int8_pc,int6_pc,fp16 --datasets wikismall(9k),shorttail(3.2k) --batch 640 --max_len 64 --metric recall_at_k.

sam: raw table pls.

jordan: quick table (rounding):
Model              Dataset       r@1    r@5    r@10
quillmark-fp16     wikismall     0.715  0.886  0.913
quillmark-int8pc   wikismall     0.710  0.884  0.912
quillmark-fp16     shorttail     0.628  0.795  0.836
quillmark-int8pc   shorttail     0.587  0.792  0.833
quillmark-int6pc   shorttail     0.606  0.793  0.834

jordan: int6_pc recovers ~1.9pp vs int8_pc on r@1 but still below fp16. r@5 stable across.

mei: consistent with other models. any diagnostics on cosine_gap / norms?

jordan: yes: median cosine_gap (top1-top2) in shorttail: fp16=0.162, int8pc=0.072, int6pc=0.118. mean norm_delta (fp16->quant) small overall but tail heavier for int8pc.

sam: examples of flips for short queries? please paste a few query traces.

jordan: sample where top1 flipped:
qA: "refund"     fp16_top=doc_45 (cos=0.74)  int8pc_top=doc_78 (cos=0.62)
qB: "billing"    fp16_top=doc_12 (cos=0.81)  int8pc_top=doc_12 (cos=0.80)
qC: "reset"      fp16_top=doc_99 (cos=0.69)  int8pc_top=doc_17 (cos=0.60)
(note: some stable ones like billing; others flip).

rachel: have you profiled kernel paths? short seq issues often due to different reduction block size / accumulator precision.

jordan: yes I profiled: for seq_len<=6 the int8 reducer uses a fast path with pairwise accumulation that increases rounding error. forcing min_pad=8 in encoder reduced int8pc r@1 gap by ~0.9pp. so padding helps.

mei: interesting. cost/latency tradeoffs? pad-to-8 will increase small-query latency and compute but not much for large batches. any cost sim?

jordan: sim with production traffic where short queries (~10% of traffic):
- baseline (int8pc all): cost_index=1.0
- pad8 variant (int8pc but pad small queries to 8): cost_index=1.03 (3% ops up), r@1 recovered ~0.9pp global
- routing fallback (cos_gap<0.12 and tokens<=5 -> fp16): cost_index=1.07 (7% ops up), r@1 recovered ~3.0pp global
- hybrid (pad8 + int6pc for short): cost_index=1.05, r@1 recovered ~2.4pp

sam: so routing gives biggest quality lift but also highest cost. pad8 is cheapest and simple.

rachel: what about trying per-cluster calibration (post-quant scale)? could be lower cost but more engineering. any quick experiments?

jordan: I tried a simple cluster-rescale on 50 clusters (kmeans on fp16 centroids) and applied per-cluster scale at eval time -> reduced flips by ~18% but introduced some instabilities for classes with few centroids. needs more careful smoothing.

mei: propose follow-up experiments: 1) three-arm run on full holdouts: baseline int8pc, int8pc+pad8, routing rule; 2) int6pc sweep for short queries; 3) cluster-rescale with smoothing. also collect human spot-check on top-200 changed hits.

jordan: plan logged in ML-ONB-2024 with attached CSV of deltas. I'll kick off the three-arm job.

eval-bot: Job scheduled: emb-eval-4319991120-three-arm (ETA ~2h)

sam: cool. if three-arm shows pad8 is ~90% of routing benefit, i'd prefer pad8 rollout first. will coordinate with infra on min-pad change if so.

rachel: also add a quick telemetry check in production to log cosine_gap distribution by token-length; that'll help monitor after rollout.

jordan: added telemetry task in ticket and included a short checklist for human eval. leaving in triage, will sync in embed-standup tomorrow. :white_check_mark: "
